To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
protozoa are more abundant in the dorsal sac than in the other two parts of the ruminal sac and that the dorsal sac is the most active site of ruminal fermentation.

(i) the distribution of protozoa in the rumen is not uniform, with the greatest proportion being in the dorsal sac, (ii) the protozoal distribution is associated with differences in pH, (iii) the protozoa are more abundant in the rumen of cows fed a diet with high barley content than with hay, and (iv) the protozoan distribution is associated with a complementary role of the protozoa with the bacteria in plant cell wall degradation.

protozoa are more abundant in the dorsal part of the rumen than in the ventral and anterior parts.
the LAP and SAB in the rumen are spatially distributed, and that the distribution is affected by diet, sampling time, and sampling site.

the rumen is not a homogeneously active organ, and protozoa are more active in the upper part of the rumen.
the distribution and activity of the LAP and SAB are not uniform in the rumen, but depend on the sampling site.
the rumen is a complex ecosystem, and that the distribution of bacteria and protozoans is not homogeneous.
